source_authority: NSW Audit Office
source_title: Youth detention is approximately seven times the daily cost of community supervision
evidence_description: The NSW Audit Office reports 2024–25 costs of $2,573.26 per young person per day in detention and $367.68 per day for community-based supervision. The ratio is approximately 7:1. Annualised, the published unit costs are about $939,883 for a detention-place year and $134,295 for a year of community supervision. This does not establish that community supervision is suitable for every young person. It establishes the scale of the economic consequence when bail/remand decisions move a person from community supervision into detention.
investigation_relevance: Deep-research finding F-091 (Snapshot 6, economic system effect branch) - see preserved/snapshot-06-2026-08-16.txt.

source_authority: NSW Audit Office
source_title: Short remand episodes are economically large
evidence_description: The Audit Office found that First Nations young people remanded and later discharged for specified non-sentenced outcomes spent an average 11 days and a median one day on remand. It reported 10,928 of 11,739 First Nations youth remand entries between January 2019 and December 2025 were later discharged for one of the listed outcomes. At the published detention unit cost, an illustrative 11-day detention episode is about $28,306. Eleven days of community supervision is about $4,044, a difference of about $24,261 if community supervision were legally and practically available as the alternative. The comparison is illustrative, not a finding that individual remand decisions were unjustified.
investigation_relevance: Deep-research finding F-092 (Snapshot 6, economic system effect branch) - see preserved/snapshot-06-2026-08-16.txt.

source_authority: Buy NSW; NSW Audit Office
source_title: The Kempsey community-program numbers are small relative to detention expenditure
evidence_description: DCJ disclosed a $934,725 five-year Kempsey Casework Support Program contract with Strong Spirit Services, including practical support for young people at risk of criminal-justice involvement and increased Aboriginal community-controlled delivery.
